notes.b1/j1/B-r1: Trace-first entry (burn line vs lightning scar, unknown winter range, disputed flame) is inventive, compact and honest about sources.
notes.b1/j1/C-r1: Fjord wyrm with seasonal table, hoard-as-midden, reused roosts and wingless lindworm variants is richly consistent, though a little long.
notes.b1/j1/A-r1: Competent but stock dragon (hoarding, horns, fire gland, thief remembered) with vague lore and some generic padding.
notes.b1/j1/C-r2: Taxonomic-record form with etymology, type skin and disputed shepherd sighting is clever, but opens with a chatty preamble and is dense.
notes.b1/j1/A-r2: Ember seam is a nice mark and the at-a-glance table and sighting log are usable, but the rest is familiar fantasy-dragon fare.
notes.b1/j1/B-r2: Grounded wingless fell dragon with band-count identification and synonyms is tidy and usable, if modest in invention.
notes.b1/j2/C-r2: Taxonomic-record form with etymology and a sheep-ledger first record is grounded and usable, but the chatty preamble and flat tone hold it back.
notes.b1/j2/A-r2: Well-organised guide with tables and the ember seam as a nice mark, yet the cinder dragon with similar-species list is fairly stock.
notes.b1/j2/B-r2: A wingless, Komodo-scaled fell wyrm with band-count individual ID and a bluff display is coherent, well-sourced and compact.
notes.b1/j2/A-r1: Competent but leans on stock dragon tropes (hoards, thermals, buckle in scat) with little new.
notes.b1/j2/C-r1: Fjord wyrm known by sign first, with seasonal table, sealers' lore and vivid measurements set beside familiar objects; rich, though long.
notes.b1/j2/B-r1: Opens with the burn line and shed skin and works back to the animal, with honest unknowns about winter; clever and usable.
notes.b1/j3/A-r2: Clean, well-structured entry with a nice ember-seam mark, but the ash-and-volcano dragon and its lookalike list are stock.
notes.b1/j3/B-r2: A wingless, Komodo-scaled fell dragon with taxonomic history and a bluffing fire display; grounded, witty and usable.
notes.b1/j3/C-r2: Draco-lizard wing ribs and a sheep-fold type record are inventive, though the chatty preamble line and length cost it a little.
notes.b1/j3/B-r1: Opens with the burn-line trace and vanishing winter records, which makes it feel like real fieldcraft.
notes.b1/j3/A-r1: Competent but generic high-fantasy dragon with hoards, thermals and horns, and little new.
notes.b1/j3/C-r1: The fjord-wyrm sign-first structure, seasonal table and sealers' similes are vivid and consistent, though it runs long.
notes.b2/j1/B-r3: Grounds fire in a burned-ewes record and a scholar who never saw one, with honest disputes over clutch size; long but earns it.
notes.b2/j1/C-r3: Rain-wyrm with a chin pearl and a ferryman's disputed measurement is vivid and well-argued, with a slightly chatty preamble.
notes.b2/j1/A-r3: Clean and usable but leans on stock dragon tropes; the hoard-as-radiator idea is the one fresh touch.
notes.b2/j1/C-r4: Compact, plate-style and consistent, but dry and visibly a Komodo/frilled-lizard remix.
notes.b2/j1/A-r4: Competent generic fantasy-bestiary entry with stock ember dragon and standard sections; padded safety and journal notes.
notes.b2/j1/B-r4: Thorough taxonomic entry with synonyms, lifecycle and lookalike table, but long and a bit encyclopedic.
notes.b2/j2/C-r4: Compact, usable, well-measured wingless monitor-dragon with a nice goatherd source note, but fairly restrained and Komodo-anchored.
notes.b2/j2/A-r4: Textbook-complete field guide format but every beat (ember glow, hoard as radiator, wyvern leg count) is the stock fantasy dragon.
notes.b2/j2/B-r4: Rich taxonomy, synonyms and seasonal movement make it feel real, though long and a bit dry with gliding-drake premise.
notes.b2/j2/A-r3: Pleasant with a few good lines (a tired dragon, remembers who took the cup), but still the familiar ember-hoard dragon.
notes.b2/j2/C-r3: A named scholar, a ferryman with a punting pole, and honest gaps give a wet river wyrm real personality and restraint.
notes.b2/j2/B-r3: Wonderful archival detail (burned ewes, four-claw lesser dragon, disputed sheen) but long and dense.
notes.b2/j3/A-r4: Clean, usable field guide layout but a stock fire-breathing hoarding dragon with generic stats.
notes.b2/j3/B-r4: Rigorous taxonomy, synonymy, lifecycle and lookalike table with Komodo and frilled-lizard anchors; slightly dry but very usable.
notes.b2/j3/C-r4: Compact plate-style entry with a nice goatherd-witness sources note; less expansive than the others.
notes.b2/j3/B-r3: Richly invented provenance (sheep-reeve's roll, disputed colour, lost specimen) and honest gaps, though dense and long.
notes.b2/j3/A-r3: Charming touches like infrasound and the remembered missing cup, but still a conventional ember dragon.
notes.b2/j3/C-r3: A wingless rain-wyrm recorded by a named surveyor with a ferryman's disputed measurement and scrupulous gaps; only the chatty preamble line detracts.
